lines.text: Father, to every son, every daughter here, help them receive the gift of Your Son, that they may know You as the Father.
And to every father here, help them give ordinary gifts to their children,
but more importantly, the greatest gift of the Son, through the Father.

child.text: Quietly thank God for one person who shared with you this year. Tomorrow, if you want to, share something small.

father.text: If you live with your child, give one ordinary good thing tonight: bread, your time. If you are far from your child, feed a hungry person and pray for your child by name.

art.prompt: Early evening in the open sandy yard of a small village church compound, under the edge of a rusty tin-roof shelter. On the right, a boy of about ten in a plain red T-shirt stands a little shyly with his arms at his sides, looking at a plate being held out to him. Facing him, a smiling girl of about eight in a yellow T-shirt holds out with both hands a colourful enamel plate of steaming orange-red jollof rice with one piece of meat on top. Behind them, softly out of focus, a woman in a yellow headwrap and an apron stirs a large black pot over a wood fire, a little smoke curling up. A warm lantern hangs from a wooden post of the shelter; the last golden sunlight comes through palm trees on the left. Only these three people are in the picture.

Late afternoon at an old round stone well on the edge of a small village of flat-roofed mud-brick houses in a dry land with a few palm trees. A woman in a simple long blue robe and head covering stands beside the well holding a clay water jar against her hip, looking down at the man with surprise and wonder. A man in a simple cream robe sits on the low stone rim of the well, seen from behind and slightly to the side so his face is not visible, one hand open toward her as he speaks. A wooden bucket on a rope rests on the rim, water glinting in it. Warm golden sun low on the right, long soft shadows on the ground, a deep teal sky. Only these two people are in the picture.

Evening inside a small one-room home with deep teal walls. At a small low wooden table, a West African father in a green patterned shirt, a steel wristwatch on his wrist, tears a round loaf of bread in two and holds out the bigger half to his small son of about seven in a yellow shirt, who reaches up for it with both hands, smiling. A single candle burns on the table beside a tin cup and a small bowl of soup. Behind them, softly out of focus, the mother in a headwrap stands by the wooden door. Warm candlelight on the father's and the boy's faces. The father and son fill the right two-thirds of the frame; a large calm area of plain teal wall on the left.

titles: My Father Gives Good Gifts | Day 5 · The Father Showed Up
He Didn't Hand You Something. He Handed You Someone.
Came For The Wrong Reason? God Will Not Send You Away
social.description:
Maybe the grown-ups around you have not given you good things, so you hold everything tight and expect nothing. Jesus says even ordinary fathers know how to give good gifts, so how much more our Father in heaven, whose best gift was His own Son.

THE WORD: Matthew 7:11 (read Matthew 7:7–11 aloud)
TONIGHT, children: quietly thank God for one person who shared with you this year. Tomorrow, if you want to, share something small.
TONIGHT, fathers: if you live with your child, give one ordinary good thing tonight: bread, your time. If you are far from your child, feed a hungry person and pray for your child by name.
SAY IT: My Father in heaven gives good gifts.
